title: Speech synthesis model
subtitle: The neural speech model that gives Helix its voice in Teams calls, a local room and produced narration.

stats.label: to first audio in the first Teams call, synthesis sharing a GPU host
speech backends behind one interface, settled by a bake-off
of the slow turn spent in synthesis while it shared the host

lede: Helix speaks in Teams calls and in a local room, and I wanted the voice to run on my own GPUs with no hosted speech service in the loop. Behind one interface the voice engine can use an 82-million-parameter open voice model in process through ONNX Runtime, and the speech synthesis model as a separate GPU service. I ran a bake-off between them, the speech synthesis model won, and I sealed it so later work could not drift the voice. the speech synthesis model is a third-party open model used as published. I wrapped it in a FastAPI streaming server in a GPU container, and the engine treats it as a remote audio component on the network.
quote: When synthesis dominated a turn on a shared host, I fixed placement and kept the model.
evidence: Speech synthesis pipelines: an open voice model wrapped in a streaming server behind a fixed seam, chosen over a second backend by a bake-off.
Latency engineering for voice AI: 776 ms to first audio in the first Teams call, and synthesis that took ~78% of a slow turn moved to a dedicated GPU host.
Performance diagnosis: a flat first-audio curve across clause lengths read as fixed server overhead and fixed by streaming rather than a faster model.
author: Corey James
